chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who went to the land of another man and cultivated it without his permission, until when the crop matured, the owner of the land came and said, 'You cultivated it without my permission, so the crop is for me and upon me is what you spent.' Is that so or not? He said, 'For the cultivator is his crop, and for the owner of the land is the rent of his land.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on crops grown on someone else's land without permission?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the principle of unjust enrichment (*istihqaq*) in agricultural tenancy, distinguishing between the laborer's right to the produce and the owner's right to the land's value. It establishes that while the cultivator retains ownership of the crop due to their effort, the landowner is entitled to fair rent (*kira'*) as compensation for the use of their property, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence on *al-muzara'ah*.
